facts.statement: Terminonatator is a genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in Saskatchewan, Canada.
facts.quote: Terminonatator (meaning "last swimmer") is a genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Saskatchewan, Canada.

facts.statement: Tamaki Sato named and described the species Terminonatator ponteixensis in 2003.
facts.quote: Tamaki Sato, who named and described the specimen in 2003, used the genus name to emphasize its lateness in the fossil record, and the species epithet ponteixensis for Ponteix.

facts.statement: Only one species, T. ponteixensis, has been described for this genus.
facts.quote: Only one species has been described: the type species T. ponteixensis.

facts.statement: As an adult, Terminonatator was small for an elasmosaurid, reaching about 7 meters in length, potentially up to 9 meters if it possessed an extremely long neck.
facts.quote: It would have been small as an adult for an elasmosaurid, at only about 7 m long, up to 9 m if it had an extremely long neck like Elasmosaurus (which had 72 neck vertebrae).

facts.statement: The preserved skull measures 26.8 cm in length but is broken near the posterior end.
facts.quote: The skull as preserved is 26.8 cm long, but is broken near the posterior end.

facts.statement: Unlike other plesiosaurs, Terminonatator had a closed pineal foramen and only nine teeth in the premaxillary bones at the snout tip, though this might be individual variation.
facts.quote: Unlike other plesiosaurs, the pineal foramen in the roof of the skull was closed, and there were only nine teeth in the premaxillary bones that form the tip of the snout instead of ten, although this could be individual variation.

facts.statement: Over 150 gastroliths, with the largest measuring 6 cm in diameter, were found within the rib cage.
facts.quote: Over 150 pebbles, representing gastroliths, were found within the rib cage; the largest has a diameter of 6 cm.

facts.statement: Terminonatator lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Terminonatator belongs to the parent group Elasmosaurinae.
Terminonatator is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
Terminonatator is classified as a reptile.
